messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: High latency SLO burn detected for /v1/generate (hosted). p95 = 1.9s (SLO 1.0s), p99 = 4.6s. Trigger: latency_alert_v2.
alice: acked in PD, jumping in. grabbing initial graphs.
ben: seeing the same on the dashboard — spike started ~1801203300, throughput normal.
carla: any recent deploys?
devops-bot: deploy: redwood-api-service v3.12.1 rolled at 1801202400 by ci-bot (no rollbacks).
alice: nothing from canary logs indicating errors. seems tail latency only.
marie: customer support flagged slow responses for three enterprise customers, tickets linked.
oncall-rotation: handing off to ben for the next 30m — oncall-rotation -> @ben.
ben: thanks — I'm primary. first hypothesis: KV cache pressure or GPU kernel path regression. ramping up detailed traces.
carla: check KV hit rates and cache eviction spikes. also check any model switchovers to larger variants.
alice: KV cache miss rate jumped from 2% to 38% starting at 1801203285.
ben: that aligns. is caching eviction due to memory pressure? show me top mem-hogs.
marie: customers impacted: acct-redwood-tech (high), beta-partner (medium), internal smoke tests, see ops-tickets link.
ben: temporary mitigation: enable aggressive prefix caching TTL extension for /v1/generate on hosted tier and route enterprise traffic to dedicated pool. can someone run the config change?
carla: prepping command. will run in staging first then prod. snippet: ```curl -X POST https://infra-api/feature_flags -d '{"prefix_cache_ttl": 120}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'```
alice: also open to throttling non-critical traffic to protect enterprise accounts. re-route suggestion: set policy route for tag:enterprise -> dedicated-fallback.
devops-bot: scaling action queued: increase dedicated-pool-3 from 4->8 gpus (estimated 70s to be ready).
ben: good. carla please apply prefix cache TTL and start dedicated pool scale. I'll update PD.
carla: applied TTL change in prod at 1801203520. response: 200.
ben: confirmed cache hit rate rising back down to ~6% at 1801203575. p95 improving but p99 still noisy (3.2s).
alice: dedicated pool scale started at 1801203540. ETA 00:01:10.
marie: informed affected customers: "we're seeing elevated latency, mitigation in progress, routing some enterprise traffic to a dedicated pool. will update shortly."
oncall-rotation: escalations: if p99 > 3s after 10m, page infra-arch escalation.
ben: pool up at 1801203612. switched enterprise routes at 1801203620.
carla: after route switch, enterprise p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.6s. hosted tier still at p99 ~2.9s for general traffic.
alice: need root cause: why did KV miss rate spike? check memc/policy churn and any config pushes to cache layer.
ben: looking at cache cluster: eviction due to max_entries reached on one hot shard; background compaction lagged because of high CPU from a cron job at 1801203270.
marie: cron job? which?
ben: nightly eval artifact cleanup job started early due to clock drift: eval-cleanup job consumed CPU and caused memcache compaction latency. scheduled at 1801203240.
carla: disabling the eval-cleanup cron instance now. disabled at 1801203650.
alice: after disabling, compaction catches up; KV misses falling. p99 trending down to 1.4s at 1801203700.
marie: updating customers again: mitigations applied, routing stable, investigating root cause.
ben: marking PD incident as acknowledged -> in-progress. will keep monitoring for 30m, then demote to post-incident review.
alice: quick follow-ups for postmortem: 1) make cache eviction alert earlier, 2) add guardrail to prevent cron job overlap, 3) add automated route to dedicated pool for enterprise if p99>2s.
carla: logging runbook steps taken in incident tracker.
oncall-rotation: handoff note: ben -> alice at 1801203750, leaving monitoring active.
ben: last check at 1801203780: p95 0.95s, p99 1.25s, KV miss 3%. closing active paging. :white_check_mark:
marie: thanks everyone. I'll create the customer impact summary for MCT and link to postmortem draft.
alice: adding ticket to retrospective board. good job team — follow-up actions assigned.
